Class Main

java.lang.Object
javafx.application.Application
application.Main
public class Main extends javafx.application.Application
Main application class and top-level controller for Battle Cat - Complete Edition.

Responsibilities:

  • Scene management – owns the primary Stage and drives transitions between the title screen, world-map level selection, and the battle scene (showMainMenu(), showLevelSelection(), showGameScene(), gameOver(String)).
  • Game loop – runs a ~60 FPS daemon thread that calls updateLogic() each tick and schedules render(GraphicsContext) on the JavaFX Application Thread via Platform.runLater(java.lang.Runnable).
  • Rendering – draws the scrollable world, all units, cannon waves, and visual effects onto a Canvas.
  • Audio – plays MP3 music through MediaPlayer (JavaFX Media). Resources are extracted to temp files at runtime because JavaFX Media requires file: URIs and cannot read jar: URIs directly.

    • showGameScene

      private void showGameScene()
      Builds and activates the in-game battle scene for the currently selected stage.

      Clears all previous state (units, buttons, effects), resets MoneyManager and BattleManager, constructs the HUD (top bar with money label, bottom tray with unit buttons, wallet-upgrade button, and cannon button), places both towers, starts stage-appropriate background music, then launches the game loop.

    • startGameThread

      private void startGameThread(javafx.scene.canvas.GraphicsContext gc)
      Spawns a daemon background thread that drives the game loop at approximately 60 FPS. Each tick calls updateLogic(), then posts render(GraphicsContext) to the JavaFX Application Thread via Platform.runLater(java.lang.Runnable). The loop exits when running is set to false.
      Parameters:
      gc - the GraphicsContext of the battle canvas to render into

    • updateLogic

      private void updateLogic()
      Advances all game state by one frame. Invoked from the game loop thread.

      Execution order each frame:

      1. If isGameOver: animate surviving units and spawn burst explosions on the destroyed tower, then return early.
      2. Advance the selected stage's enemy-spawn schedule.
      3. Tick MoneyManager; post a HUD-button affordability update to the JavaFX thread.
      4. Update every unit; remove dead non-tower units from the board and from BattleManager.
      5. Advance all active CannonWaves; remove finished ones.
      6. On the first frame a tower reaches 0 HP: zero out all allied units on that side, set the result string, start the result jingle, and begin the 150-frame game-over countdown.
      7. While the countdown is active: emit burst particles every 12 frames and shake the dead tower every 3 frames. When the counter reaches 0, call gameOver(String).

    • render

      private void render(javafx.scene.canvas.GraphicsContext gc)
      Draws the current frame onto the battle canvas. Must be called on the JavaFX Application Thread.

      Drawing order:

      1. Stage background image, or a solid Color.WHITESMOKE fallback.
      2. Each unit: towers are drawn with their HP overlay and an optional horizontal shake; regular units use their current sprite and Y-offset, with a smaller soul sprite substituted when dead.
      3. All active CannonWave projectiles.
      4. UFOCat explosion particles via EffectManager.
      5. Tower-destruction burst particles.
      Parameters:
      gc - the GraphicsContext of the battle canvas

    • showPauseOverlay

      private void showPauseOverlay()
      Pauses the game loop and shows a semi-transparent overlay with CONTINUE and RETURN TO MAP buttons. Pressing CONTINUE removes the overlay and resumes the loop. Pressing RETURN TO MAP stops music and navigates to level selection.

    • openPlayer

      private javafx.scene.media.MediaPlayer openPlayer(String path)
      Loads a classpath MP3 resource into a MediaPlayer.

      JavaFX Media requires a file: URI and cannot read jar: URIs, so the resource is first copied to a temporary file. The temp file is registered for deletion on JVM exit. Volume is set to 15 % of maximum to prevent audio clipping.

      Parameters:
      path - classpath-relative path to the MP3 (e.g. "/music/001.mp3")
      Returns:
      a configured MediaPlayer ready for playback, or null if the resource cannot be found or loaded

    • startMenuMusic

    • playResultMusic

      private void playResultMusic(String path)
      Stops the stage music and plays a one-shot win/lose result jingle. The jingle plays once with no loop and stops naturally at the end.

      This method may be called from the game loop thread; it wraps all MediaPlayer operations inside Platform.runLater(java.lang.Runnable) to satisfy JavaFX's thread requirement.

      Parameters:
      path - classpath-relative path to the MP3 result track (e.g. "/music/008.mp3" for win, "/music/009.mp3" for lose)

    • showMainMenu

      private void showMainMenu()
      Builds and displays the title screen with a START button. Stops the game loop if one is running and starts menu background music.

    • showLevelSelection

      private void showLevelSelection()
      Builds and displays the world-map level-selection screen. Five clickable stage pins are positioned at their geographic locations on the map image. Clicking a pin sets selectedStage and calls showGameScene(). A BACK button returns to the title screen. Menu music continues (or restarts) on this screen.

    • spawnTowerBurst

      private void spawnTowerBurst(Tower tower)
      Adds a new TowerBurstEffect at a random position within the given tower's sprite bounds. Called every 12 frames during the post-destruction countdown to simulate the tower crumbling.
      Parameters:
      tower - the tower whose bounds are used to position the burst effect

    • gameOver

      private void gameOver(String resultText)
      Sets isGameOver and posts a game-over overlay to the JavaFX Application Thread. The overlay shows the result text and a RETURN TO MAP button that stops music and navigates to level selection. The render loop continues after this call so burst animations keep playing.
      Parameters:
      resultText - the result message to display ("YOU WIN!" or "YOU LOSE!")
